label: STOPP H3
title: Long-term NSAID for osteoarthritis, paracetamol not tried
statement: Long-term use of NSAID (>3 months) for symptom relief of osteoarthritis pain where paracetamol has not been tried (simple analgesics preferable and usually as effective for pain relief and safer).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: Review prolonged systemic NSAID use for osteoarthritis pain and whether paracetamol has been tried. For knee osteoarthritis, paracetamol generally provides less pain relief than NSAIDs but may be considered when NSAID harms are a concern. Australian guidance differs: a paracetamol trial is optional before an oral NSAID for knee or hip osteoarthritis (RACGP, 2018).

medicine_groups.name: NSAIDs, the anti-inflammatory pain medicines

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, suppositories and injections count. Skin gels, creams and eye drops do not count, for example Voltaren Emulgel. Aspirin is not in this group. Nurofen Plus and Panafen Plus are ibuprofen with codeine. Nuromol and Maxigesic are ibuprofen with paracetamol. Arthrotec is diclofenac with misoprostol. Vimovo is naproxen with esomeprazole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

Panadol Children's Drops 1 Month to 2 Years

medicine_groups.note: Combination packs that contain paracetamol, such as Panadeine, Panadeine Forte, Maxigesic and Nuromol, also show paracetamol was supplied. Panadeine and Panadeine Forte are paracetamol with codeine. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Lemsip Cold and Flu, Lemsip Cold and Flu Liquid Capsule, Lemsip Max, Lemsip Max Cold and Flu, Panadol Cold and Flu Hot and Panadol Cold and Flu Max are pack names. Check the recorded active ingredients. A combination or a supply for cold symptoms alone does not establish a simple paracetamol trial for osteoarthritis pain. If the formulation or trial is unclear, report a possible finding and ask what was tried.

rule_for_models: For a person aged 65 or older, assess the first systemic Group A NSAID supply more than 90 days after the course starts, with no gap over 60 days. Leave age eligibility unconfirmed if unknown. Flag regular use for osteoarthritis pain when the patient had not tried paracetamol alone by that date. Cite the NSAID course, the diagnosis and the trial history. Give no finding if simple Group B paracetamol was supplied by that date unless it was solely for another purpose. A documented earlier trial also clears the finding, including paracetamol bought elsewhere. A later trial does not clear an earlier finding. A combination alone does not establish a trial. If no exclusion applies and regular use, the diagnosis, the indication or a prior trial is uncertain, report a possible finding naming what is missing. Give no finding if osteoarthritis is excluded or the NSAID was used solely for another condition. For an otherwise qualifying course, ask what the NSAID treated only if its purpose is unclear. Ask about actual use only if the directions and record leave regular use uncertain. Apply each answer only to that course. Intermittent use alone gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why the NSAID was started, whether paracetamol was tried before the record began, and paracetamol bought without a prescription. Also how often the NSAID is really taken and medicines supplied by another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether paracetamol has been tried for the osteoarthritis pain, and whether the NSAID can be stopped or reduced.
